..title
A resolution approving an amendment to an intergovernmental agreement and two new intergovernmental agreements by and between the Tennessee Department of Transportation (“TDOT”) and the Metropolitan Government, acting by and through the Nashville Department of Transportation and Multimodal Infrastructure (“NDOT”), for roadway and infrastructure improvements to Cowan Street/Marine Drive and James Robertson Parkway. (Proposal No. 2026M-061AG-001 and 2026M-062AG-001).
..body
WHEREAS, pursuant to Resolution No. RS2021-909, the Metropolitan Council approved an agreement (the “Connection Agreement”) between TDOT and the Metropolitan Government for roadway and infrastructure improvements to Cowan Street and a connection from East Nashville from the River North area under Interstate 24; and
WHEREAS, as set forth in the agreement (the “Cowan/Marine Agreement”) attached as Exhibit 1, NDOT and TDOT propose to jointly pursue and share in the cost of roadway and infrastructure improvements to Cowan Street and Marine Drive, and
WHEREAS the improvements contemplated in the Cowan/Marine Agreement supersede those contemplated in the Connection Agreement; and 
WHEREAS, as provided in Exhibit 2, NDOT and TDOT propose to amend the Connection Agreement to conform with the Cowan/Marine Agreement; and
WHEREAS, as set forth in the agreement attached as Exhibit 3, NDOT and TDOT propose to jointly pursue and share in the cost of roadway and infrastructure improvements to James Robertson Parkway; and
WHEREAS, as set forth in the agreement attached as Exhibit 1, NDOT and TDOT propose to jointly pursue and share in the cost of roadway and infrastructure improvements to Cowan Street and Marine Drive, and
WHEREAS, as set forth in the agreement attached as Exhibit 2, NDOT and TDOT propose to jointly pursue and share in the cost of roadway and infrastructure improvements to James Robertson Parkway, and
WHEREAS, the Cowan Street/Marine Drive and James Robertson Parkway improvements will significantly improve mobility and transportation options on the East Bank; and
WHEREAS, as planning advances for the East Bank infrastructure and roadway improvements, continued connectivity between the East Bank project area and adjacent communities remains an important consideration; and
WHEREAS, the development of a proposed multimodal connection between the East Bank project area and the Ellington Parkway pedestrian bridge will help maintain connectivity between adjacent communities, and its initial planning and design work has been approved; and
WHEREAS, NDOT has committed to partner with the Metropolitan Department of Parks and Recreation, the Metropolitan Department of Planning, the East Bank Development Authority, and other relevant departments and agencies to analyze and prepare preliminary designs for this connection; and
WHEREAS, Tennessee Code Annotated § 12-9-104(a)(2)(b) authorizes the Metropolitan Government to enter into intergovernmental agreements with the State of Tennessee by resolution; and
WHEREAS, it is in the interest of the Metropolitan Government of Nashville and Davidson County that the intergovernmental agreements be approved.
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE COUNCIL OF THE METROPOLITAN GOVERNMENT OF NASHVILLE AND DAVIDSON COUNTY:
Section 1. That the amendment to the Connection Agreement, attached as Exhibit 2, and the intergovernmental agreements between the Tennessee Department of Transportation and the Metropolitan Government of Nashville and Davidson County, by and through the Nashville Department of Transportation and Multimodal Infrastructure, attached as Exhibits 1 and 2 3, are approved.
Section 2. That the Metropolitan Mayor is authorized to execute the intergovernmental agreements and such other customary and reasonable documents as necessary to carry out the improvements to Cowan Street, Marine Drive, and James Robertson Parkway as the agreements contemplate.
Section 3. That any amendments, renewals, or extension of the terms of the agreements may be approved by resolution of the Metropolitan Council.
Section 4. The Metropolitan Council hereby expresses its support for the Nashville Department of Transportation and Multimodal Infrastructure to conduct the analysis of and preliminary design work for a proposed multimodal connection between the East Bank project area and the Ellington Parkway pedestrian bridge, in coordination with the Metropolitan Department of Parks and Recreation, the Metropolitan Department of Planning, the East Bank Development Authority, and other relevant departments and agencies.
Section 5. That this resolution shall take effect from and after its adoption, the welfare of the Metropolitan Government of Nashville and Davidson County requiring it.
..Agenda Analysis
Analysis

This resolution approves two intergovernmental agreements between the Nashville Department of Transportation (“NDOT”) and the Tennessee Department of Transportation (“TDOT”) for roadway and infrastructure improvements. The first agreement concerns improvements to Cowan Street and Marine Drive. The second agreement concerns improvements to James Robertson Parkway. 

Tennessee Code Annotated § 12-9-104(a)(2)(b) authorizes the Metropolitan Government to enter into intergovernmental agreements with the State of Tennessee by resolution.

Cowan Street and Marine Drive

According to an attached memorandum of understanding between TDOT, the Metropolitan Government, and the East Bank Development Authority (“EBDA”), the scope of work is as follows:

Replacement of all Interstate 24 bridges and the related ramp bridge
Extension of Marine Drive from Dickerson Pike to Cowan Street under Interstate 24
Widening Cowan Street from Spring Street to Marine Drive
Improvements for Dickerson Pike from Meridian Street to Grace Street
Installing a new 72-inch regional stormwater trunk line.

TDOT is responsible for all phases of the project, except for the final striping on Marine Drive and Cowan Street, the acquisition of right-of-way for a proposed shared access roadway, the installation of all transit equipment, and the removal and reinstallation of the existing buffalo statues in the middle of Dickerson Pike. The parties will work to complete the Cowan Street phase by June 30, 2029, the Interstate 24 bridges phase by September 30, 2029, and the Marine Drive phase by September 30, 2030.

The estimated total cost of the project is $208,000,000. NDOT will be responsible for 50 percent of the project cost, or $104,000,000, over the course of four payments. The term of the agreement begins upon approval of all required parties. The agreement may be terminated by TDOT with 30 days’ notice, following a required conference with NDOT or by either party for cause.

This agreement separately amends an agreement between TDOT and NDOT, as approved by Resolution No. RS2021-909. This amendment replaces the text of the agreement for a Cleveland Street Extension and Bike/Pedestrian Connectivity from East Nashville to River North Development with the agreement for Marine Drive, from Dickerson Pike to Cowan Street under Interstate 24.

James Robertson Parkway

According to an attached memorandum of understanding between TDOT, the Metropolitan Government, and the East Bank Development Authority (“EBDA”), the scope of work is as follows:

Repaving and lowering of James Robertson Parkway from Victory Memorial Bridge to Interstate Drive. This includes 78 feet of pavement from curb to curb, 2.5-feet of curb and gutters, 4 feet of furnishing area, and 14 feet of sidewalks of each side of the curb.
Constructing a 12-foot shoulder on the south side of James Robertson Parkway between 1st Street and 2nd Street. 
Constructing tie-ins to South 2nd Street from Jackson Robertson Parkway to Woodland Street
Installing a new 72-inch regional stormwater trunk line.

TDOT is responsible for all phases of the project. A full-time NDOT employee would supervise the various phases of the project The parties will work to substantially complete the project by July 31, 2029.

The estimated cost of the project is a combined $185,000,000. TDOT would fund the section of the project from Victory Memorial Bridge to 1st Street, in an amount not to exceed $85,000,000. NDOT would fund the section of the project from 1st Street to Interstate Drive and the 2nd Street segment, in an amount not to exceed $100,000,000. These funds would be paid from NDOT to TDOT in four installments.

The term of the agreement begins upon approval of all required parties. The agreement may be terminated by TDOT with 30 days’ notice, following a required conference with NDOT or by either party for cause.

Fiscal Note: This resolution includes two Local Agency Project Agreements. 

The new road construction agreement for Marine Drive, from SR11 (US-41, Dickerson Pike) to Cowan Street under I-24 has a total estimated project cost of $208,000,000, as defined in Exhibit A.  The Metropolitan Government will be responsible for fifty percent (50%) of the total estimated project cost, to be paid in four installments. The first installment is $34,000,000; second installment is $30,000,000; third installment is $30,000,000; and the fourth installment will be the remaining cost. Metro will be responsible for maintenance and operation of any installed traffic signal, lighting and replacement of solar panels, batteries, lights and lenses on solar power devices.

The bridge rehabilitation agreement for James Robertson Parkway (SR6, US41), from Victory Memorial Bridge to Interstate Drive, has a total estimated project cost of $185,000,000. The Metropolitan Government’s share of the estimated project cost, as defined in Exhibit A, is $100,000 but not to exceed $119,000,000, to be paid in four installments. This includes fifty percent (50%) of Professional Engineer–Design (PEDesign) at $6,890,000; rightofway cost of $41,619,500; construction cost of $48,079,500; and fifty percent (50%) of construction engineering and inspection (CEI) at $3,411,000. The first installment is $25,000,000; the second installment is $25,000,000; the third installment is $25,000,000; and the final payment at project closeout will be either the Metropolitan Government’s total cost if the total cost is less than $119,000,000, or $44,000 if it exceeds $119,000,000. The Metropolitan Government will not be responsible for additional costs if its share of the project cost exceeds $119,000,000 but will be responsible for maintenance and operation of any installed traffic signals and lighting, as well as replacement of solar panels, batteries, lights, and lenses on solarpowered devices.
